tool_input.message:
Silent-failure review of feat/z-spec-state-machines vs main is complete: 4 findings (1 HIGH, 2 MEDIUM, 1 LOW), none critical. All primary error-propagation questions check out.

VERIFIED CORRECT (the questions you asked):
- Loop propagation: Makefile:151-155 uses `fuzz "$$f" || status=1; ... exit $$status`. A second-file failure after a first-file success still fails make, and the loop continues so all failing specs are reported in one run. set -e/pipefail are irrelevant: one shell invocation, explicit status accumulation, no pipes.
- Local skip is loud: Makefile:147 prints an explicit `*** fuzz not installed -- SKIPPING ***` line with remediation, exit 0. Stdout not stderr, but announced per-run. Matches the documented design.
- CI cannot silently skip on a missing binary: Makefile:142-146 hard-fails to stderr when CI is set (GitHub Actions always sets CI=true). This also catches the "install step succeeded but fuzz absent" case.
- Workflow install path fails loudly: default `bash -e` step shell; checkout action, apt-get, and install.sh each fail the job on nonzero. I verified against the PINNED tag (punt-labs/z-spec v0.20.5, which is what CI runs — the local z-spec checkout is 6 commits ahead): install.sh:699-710 converts a fuzz build failure under --fuzz-only into hard exit 1, and its install prefix ($HOME/.local, install.sh:408) matches the workflow's GITHUB_PATH export, which does take effect in the later `make fuzz-check` step.

FINDINGS:

F1 HIGH — Vacuous pass in CI when spec detection matches nothing. Makefile:138-140: the empty-FUZZ_SPECS branch prints one stdout line and exits 0, including in CI. Four specs exist on this branch, so an empty match in CI can only mean detection broke (e.g. preamble refactored into a shared .sty so `\usepackage{fuzz}` leaves the .tex files, or files renamed/moved). CI would print "nothing to type-check" inside a green job. The missing-binary case gets a CI hard-fail; this equivalent broken-gate case does not. Fix: inside the empty branch, `if [ -n "$$CI" ]; then echo "detection matched zero files -- gate broken" >&2; exit 1; fi` before the local exit 0.

F2 MEDIUM — Non-recursive glob contradicts the comment. Makefile:135 globs `docs/*.tex` only; the comment at Makefile:102-103 claims "a new spec landing under docs/" is picked up. A spec at docs/specs/foo.tex is silently excluded with NO message (other files still match, so the announced empty-case never fires). Fix: `grep -rl --include='*.tex' 'usepackage{fuzz}' docs` or correct the comment to "directly in docs/".

F3 MEDIUM — Pattern misses the bracketed-options form. Makefile:135 matches literal `usepackage{fuzz}` but not `\usepackage[opts]{fuzz}`. The option form is idiomatic in these very files (spec-hook-gates.tex:20 and :24 use it for geometry/hyperref). A future author adding an option to the fuzz package silently drops that file from the gate. Fix: `grep -El 'usepackage(\[[^]]*\])?\{fuzz\}'` or document the bare form as a required convention.

F4 LOW — `2>/dev/null` on the detection grep (Makefile:135) also suppresses a permission/IO error on an individual spec, converting an unreadable file into a silent exclusion. Fixing F1 caps the damage.

No findings in docs/development.md or in the workflow beyond F1. .tex spec content and .punt-labs/ethos bookkeeping excluded per scope.
